articles.title: Google's Genie 4: Interactive Worlds Now Talk Back, and You Can Steer Them Live
articles.excerpt: Google DeepMind has announced Genie 4, a new world model that generates explorable, photorealistic interactive worlds in real time from a text prompt or an image. Announced on October 27, 2026, it is…
articles.body: Google DeepMind has announced Genie 4, a new world model that generates explorable, photorealistic interactive worlds in real time from a text prompt or an image. Announced on October 27, 2026, it is available as a research preview for trusted testers, rolling out first to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and to early-access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, with a waitlist open for others. The headline change is sound. Genie 4 is DeepMind's first real-time world model with native audio: music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue are generated simultaneously with the world itself. Characters in the scene can converse and react in real time. That turns a world from something you watch into something you can talk to. The second change is duration.

articles.title: Does Turtle Trading Still Work? What 6.7 Years Showed
articles.excerpt: The short version. On the data I have, no: the original Turtle trading rules lost 37.9% on 11 Exness markets and 57.7% on 26, from January 2020 to September 2026, with the code checked three ways. But…
articles.body: The short version. On the data I have, no: the original Turtle trading rules lost 37.9% on 11 Exness markets and 57.7% on 26, from January 2020 to September 2026, with the code checked three ways. But 6.7 years is a short window for a trend system, and the result is mostly one-sided: long trades made money in every market group, short trades lost in every group. The tempting fix, dropping the shorts, is exactly the kind of decision you can't make after seeing the results. Here's what I think the test does show, what it doesn't, and what I didn't do. This is the last of 5 parts: the 1983 experiment , the rules , the simulator , the results . Does Turtle trading still work in 2026? Not as published, on Exness CFDs, from 2020 to 2026.

articles.title: How I Built a C# MCP Server with Single-Use Order Approvals
articles.excerpt: Giving an assistant a tool for reading orders is straightforward. Giving it a cancellation tool raises a different question: who authorizes the change? I wanted to explore that boundary without treati…
articles.body: Giving an assistant a tool for reading orders is straightforward. Giving it a cancellation tool raises a different question: who authorizes the change? I wanted to explore that boundary without treating a model-generated confirmation as permission. I built dotnet-mcp-orders-server , a small .NET 8 MCP server exposing fictional orders. It offers list, lookup and cancellation tools over stdio. Cancellation requires an independently recorded approval for one action and one exact order, with an expiration time. The project has 12 tests, all passing in GitHub CI. Those tests exercise the tool methods and approval behavior; they do not establish an interactive connection with Claude or ChatGPT. Here is how I built the approval flow and where its guarantees end.

articles.title: A/B Testing Trading Rules: The 52 Rejected Trades That Changed My Mind
articles.excerpt: The Question a Filter Should Answer A pullback filter sits in front of an entry signal and decides which setups are allowed through. The usual debate goes like this: the strict variant looks cleaner o…
articles.body: The Question a Filter Should Answer A pullback filter sits in front of an entry signal and decides which setups are allowed through. The usual debate goes like this: the strict variant looks cleaner on the equity curve, the relaxed variant trades more, and someone argues the extra trades are "noise." That argument is almost never tested. It is asserted from the shape of the curve. The right question is narrower: what happens to the trades that exist only because of the relaxed rule? If that incremental set has positive expectancy, the strict filter is not cleaning up noise. It is deleting the strategy's core. In the case I worked through, the strict rule rejected 52 trades that the relaxed rule took.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart
articles.excerpt: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic 'string of pearls,' a unique celestial relic left by a supernova witnessed by humanity around 850 years ago, which has a zombie star at its heart.
articles.body: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic "string of pearls," a unique celestial relic left by a supernova explosion that humanity witnessed around 850 years ago. That is thanks to the most detailed observation of the dandelion-shaped chains of gas and supernova debris that comprise Pa 30, the only supernova remnant of its type observed in the Milky Way . What makes Pa 30 even more unique is that it has a rare "zombie star" at its heart. Supernovas like the one that created Pa 30 are called Type Ia supernovas; they happen when a dead star called a white dwarf overfeeds on a companion star like a cosmic vampire. This overfeeding triggers a runaway nuclear explosion that usually destroys the white dwarf.

articles.title: Cowboy Space unveils 'Big Iron' rocket to launch 20,000 AI data centers
articles.excerpt: Cowboy Space just gave us our first look at its "Big Iron" rocket, which the company will use to build its AI data center constellation. Big Iron's debut is targeted for late 2028.
articles.body: PALO ALTO, Calif. — Cowboy Space just showed us how it plans to become a big player in the final frontier. The California-based company, which is run by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt, intends to operate a constellation of 20,000 AI data centers in low Earth orbit (LEO). It will build those satellites in house and launch them on a homegrown rocket — a vehicle Cowboy Space unveiled here on Monday night (Oct. 26), at an event it called "Big Sky Rising." "It's a fundamentally novel approach to rocketry in the modern era, in our opinion," Bhatt said during the event. "The idea is that you have a two-stage rocket where the upper stage of the rocket itself transforms into the satellite." Big Iron's first stage will be reusable.

articles.title: November full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Beaver Moon
articles.excerpt: Your guide to November's full Beaver Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
articles.body: The November full moon reaches maximum illumination at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk sits opposite the sun in Earth's sky, appearing fully lit by its rays. November's full moon is traditionally known as the " Beaver Moon ", because it rises around the time when the small mammals take refuge in their dens, having stored enough food to survive the long winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . The Nov. 24 full moon also happens to be the first of three consecutive " supermoons ". The non-scientific term is often bestowed on full moons that occur when the natural satellite is within 90% of perigee, when the moon is closest to Earth in its elliptical orbit.
